title: Orchestrate GPU nodepool claim mapping and IAM shard bridge
author: Diego Ramirez
description: Motivation: Private deployments need deterministic GPU allocation and least-privilege IAM wiring when multiple tenants claim ephemeral GPU capacity across AZs. This PR introduces two coordinated Terraform modules and migration hooks: (1) modules/gpu/claim-mapper - a declarative mapping layer that reconciles TenantLease CR annotations into nodepool placement metadata and TF state pointers; (2) modules/iam/shard-bridge - a scoped role-binding factory that generates per-tenant IAM roles and cross-account role-bridges for cloud providers. The implementation also includes a tfstate layout adjustment (tenant-lease-index) to minimize lock contention during parallel applies and a small controller-side annotation convention used by the installer to encode preferred AZ affinity. Design: claim-mapper exposes inputs for tenant_id, gpu_profile, preferred_azs, and lease_duration; it outputs nodepool selectors and a stable tfstate key for the lease. The shard-bridge takes tenant_id and service_accounts and emits minimal IAM roles with a managed trust policy template to support short-lived credentials. Migration & upgrade plan: this change introduces an inheritable tfstate prefix; a migration tool (scripts/tfstate-migrate/lease-mapper) is included to stitch existing tenant leases into the new index with a dry-run mode. For upgrades we run: 1) dry migrate mapping on staging 2) land shard-bridge with canary tenant 3) promote mapping across remaining tenants; nothing is applied to nodepools until a controlled apply with tenant gating. Testing & validation: included unit tests for tfvars rendering, an integration harness that runs terraform plan against a mocked backend, and an e2e smoke that provisions a single canary nodepool in the QA VPC. Performance: in local bench runs mapping reconcile reduced apply time for concurrent tenant claims by ~38% (measured across 16 simulated tenants). Security: IAM roles created by shard-bridge follow least-privilege template and rotate role names via immutable suffix to avoid accidental permission reuse. Files changed (high level): modules/gpu/claim-mapper/{main.tf,outputs.tf,variables.tf}, modules/iam/shard-bridge/{main.tf,roles.tpl,variables.tf}, scripts/tfstate-migrate/lease-mapper (Go binary + README), examples/tenant-canary/{vars.tf,README.md}, docs/upgrade/lease-indexing.md, charts/installer/values.yaml (small flag to enable new annotation convention). Backwards compatibility: the modules are opt-in via a new module flag enable_claim_indexing=false by default; migration tool will not modify live state unless run with --apply. Rollback plan: migration tool supports snapshot rollback and the installer adds a feature flag to short-circuit claim-mapper behavior. Related work: builds on ENG-1622 (tenant lease refactor) and complements redwood-terraform changes for tfstate anchoring.

upgrade_instructions: 1) Ensure feature flag enable_claim_indexing=false in installer values.yaml before upgrade
2) Run scripts/tfstate-migrate/lease-mapper --dry-run --staging to validate mapping output
3) Flip enable_claim_indexing=true for a single canary tenant and apply in a controlled window
4) Run migration with --apply for remaining tenants in small batches (recommended 5 at a time)
5) Monitor installer console for claim mapping stats and reversion signals; rollback using lease-mapper snapshot if necessary
release_notes: Added opt-in claim-mapper and IAM shard-bridge Terraform modules to improve parallel apply performance and enforce least-privilege IAM bridging for tenant GPU claims. Includes migration tool with dry-run and rollback. Disabled by default; opt-in via installer values. See docs/upgrade/lease-indexing.md for detailed procedure.
